summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 14.3 to Angular 15.2 using `ng update @angular/core@15 @angular/cli@15`, and bumped @ngrx/* from 14 to 15 to match. Angular's own migrations handled the removal of `relativeLinkResolution`, the `renderModule` re-export in main.server.ts, the obsolete `require.context` block in test.ts, and the tsconfig target/useDefineForClassFields change. `npm install` and `npm run build` pass; `npm run test` still fails for the same pre-existing reason as at baseline.
changes: src/app/app.module.ts: removed the deprecated `relativeLinkResolution: 'legacy'` router option (migration).
src/main.server.ts: dropped the `renderModule` re-export, now provided by the CLI (migration).
src/test.ts: removed the `require.context` test loader, no longer needed by the Karma builder (migration).
tsconfig.json: target ES2022 + `useDefineForClassFields: false`; src/tsconfig.server.json: dropped its `target` override (migration).
Regenerated package-lock.json: the lockfile produced during `ng update` was missing the root `webpack` entry, which broke `ng build` with "Cannot find module 'webpack'".
manual_followups: Tests still fail (as at baseline) because the `test` target in angular.json lists the stylesheet as "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so Karma aborts with "Can't resolve 'styles.css'". Fixing that path is outside this hop but would let the suite run.
src/main.server.ts still exports `renderModuleFactory`, which is removed in Angular 16 - it will need replacing with `renderModule` in a later hop.
Deprecated/legacy devDeps remain (tslint, codelyzer, protractor, node-sass, core-js 2, @types/node 12); they are unused by the required checks but should be retired.
